I've made my way through a handful of really divisive, unhealthy INTJ forums and it took me quite some time to find a community I felt was mature an even-handed enough to really enjoy. What are some common problems we should strive to avoid as this community matures?
What pitfalls should we strive to avoid here that other INTJ communities have fallen prey to?
I think that it is inevitable and part of the growing experience as an INTJ. Just lead the younger ones to the calmer path.

I'll throw in my two cents as well: As much as INTJs tend to be firm in their convictions, even stubbornly so, I'd like to see members strive to understand others by asking questions in an attempt to understand instead of making assertions, ending the conversation.

That, and I'd like to see more discussions surrounding cognitive functions :) The sixteen profiles are very interesting, but digging deeper into the various functions has been fascinating. It brings more life and depth of understanding to the various temperaments.

I recall some of your posts on Reddit, it interests me that you've chosen the same name.

I only have one thing to say regarding your topic. We need an INTJ guide to introduce them and bring them new/young INTJ's up to speed on what we expect and tolerate. Hopefully this can help prevent an "Eternal September" effect.

As /u/FJP mentioned DAEs, my other concern is the development of a hive mind and the submission of low-effort posts (e.g. image macro of what an INTJ looks like with the ENFP around).

Some communities really played up the stereotypes and criticized those who did not fit the bill or lacked an "INTJ mindset". Nobody's gonna fit the type descriptions to a tee and there are people of different types that will occasionally wander in and add to the sub/discussion. Contribution points are not given or taken away for being on certain sides of an argument but for having something that drives discussion.

I do realise that some younger INTJs would need guidance but that should never excuse poor/close-minded behaviour and low-quality posts to run rampant throughout the sub. We need to clearly define our standards and perhaps manage the type of posts we have by scheduling them or restricting them. As for what type of posts, we'll have to see as there isn't much content in here yet.

I personally am very against low-effort image posts, especially ones that play up to the "mastermind" or "heartless robot" stereotype. They act as another form of DAE and would encourage a negative and somewhat elitist mindset in underdeveloped INTJs ("I'm not an asocial jerk, I'm just part of the 3% who actually gets it!"). Some of them are satirical and funny but there's a fine line between that and ego-fodder. Previous communities have shown that those posts tend to fall into the latter category. However, if it was something like an image with a quote in it plus discussion started by the OP in the comments then I'd be okay with it.
